report.verdict: A senior backend engineer with a strong ledger project, but recent jobs leave the work mostly unstated.
write_up: Senior backend engineer working on payouts and ledger services, with an open-source reconciliation project. It's common to see a profile with a default headline, a generic About and little under the jobs. Here, a recruiter knows your field but has to guess what you did at Northwind Pay.

The ledger-recon project is the model: it names the library, Go, 1,200 GitHub stars and three payment companies using it. That work is already on your profile, so bring it into your About rather than starting from scratch.
Start with the Northwind Pay job, then fill in Kestrel Labs and update the headline and About. A recruiter hiring for payments backend work could then see your contributions alongside the library.

cards.line: Senior Backend Engineer at Northwind Pay
cards.cannot_tell: This repeats your title but leaves out the payments work. Put payouts and ledger services beside the role so a recruiter can see your specialty.
cards.example: Senior Backend Engineer | Payouts and ledger services | Go, PostgreSQL
cards.question: Which parts of payouts and ledger services do you work on?

cards.line: Passionate engineer with a track record of delivering scalable solutions. I enjoy hard problems and working with great teams.
cards.cannot_tell: 'Scalable solutions' could describe almost any engineer. Your ledger-recon project names the library and the companies using it, so bring that work up here.
cards.example: I'm a Senior Backend Engineer at Northwind Pay, working on payouts and ledger services. My projects include ledger-recon, an open-source ledger reconciliation library in Go used by three payment companies.
cards.question: What part did you play in creating or maintaining ledger-recon?

cards.line: Worked on payouts and ledger services.
cards.cannot_tell: One sentence leaves your contribution to payouts and ledger services unclear. Name the parts you worked on, what you did and which tools you used.
cards.example: Worked on payouts and ledger services, including [which parts and what you did], using [tools].
cards.question: Which parts of payouts and ledger services were yours, what did you do on them, and which tools did you use?

cards.line: The Software Engineer job at Kestrel Labs has no description.
cards.cannot_tell: The title doesn't say what you built or maintained. Terms such as APIs, data models and services have nothing under this job to match, if those were part of your work.
cards.example: [What you built or maintained] for [who used it], using [tools or languages].
cards.question: At Kestrel Labs, did you work on APIs, data models or services? What did you build or maintain, and who used it?

cards.line: Open-source ledger reconciliation library in Go. 1,200 GitHub stars, used by three payment companies.
cards.cannot_tell: Keep this as the model. It names the library's purpose and language, then shows its reach without making a recruiter guess what it is.

fit.why: Your headline and current title name senior backend engineering, and your Northwind Pay job and ledger-recon project point to payments work.
fit.level: senior, the Senior Backend Engineer title at Northwind Pay
fit.note: 'Senior Backend Engineer' is in your headline and current title. 'Payouts' is in the Northwind Pay description, and 'ledger reconciliation' is in your project. 'Go' is in your top skills and project; 'PostgreSQL' is in your top skills. Transaction processing, distributed systems and APIs aren't named on your profile. If they describe your work, add them to the Northwind Pay description, with distributed systems in your About if it ties your work together. Move payouts and ledger services into your headline.
